item.title: 🟠 New Linux pedit COW Exploit Enables Root Access by Poisoning Cached Binaries
item.description:
Why this matters: Leadership context — useful for risk, budget, and vendor conversations.
A flaw in the Linux kernel's traffic-control subsystem can let a local unprivileged user gain root on affected systems. CVE-2026-46331, nicknamed "pedit COW," is an out-of-bounds write in the packet-editing action (act_pedit) that corrupts shared page-cache memory. item.title: 🟠 Amazon Q Developer Flaw Could Let Malicious Repos Run Code via MCP Configs
item.description:
Why this matters: Credential/phishing risk — reinforce MFA and user awareness training.
A high-severity flaw in Amazon Q Developer let a malicious repository run commands and steal a developer's cloud credentials. The path was short: a developer opens the repo, trusts the workspace, and Amazon Q does the rest. Amazon has patched it. item.title: 🟠 CISA Adds Exploited PTC Windchill RCE Flaw to KEV as Web Shell Attacks Continue
item.description:

item.title: 🟠 New DirtyClone Linux Kernel Flaw Lets Local Users Gain Root via Cloned Packets
item.description:
Why this matters: Privilege escalation risk — review local admin exposure and endpoint controls.
DirtyClone is a new Linux kernel privilege escalation in the DirtyFrag family. JFrog Security Research published a working exploit walkthrough for the flaw on June 25, the first public demonstration for this variant. item.title: 🔴 Miasma Malware Targets npm Packages and GitHub Actions in Supply Chain Attack
item.description:
Why this matters: Supply chain risk — audit third-party dependencies and vendor access.
